operations.name: Dedicated Facing — Left End
operations.setup_note: Hold the normalized blank on its raw OD and finish the -Z end face as a temporary axial reference. This is the first loading of the dedicated facing stage; datum A is not yet established.

operations.name: Dedicated Facing and Bore Starting — Right End
operations.setup_note: Reverse blank against faced end and finish face opposite end to overall length 27.0 mm across the annulus wall.

operations.name: CNC Rough Turn and Bore — Right End
operations.setup_note: Grip rolled ring blank in bored soft jaws, rough external diameters, then rough bore ID from Ø110 to Ø116.5 and counterbore Ø129.2, followed by finish boring.

operations.name: CNC Rough Turn and Counterbore — Left End
operations.setup_note: Reverse onto the prepared right-hand rim using low-pressure soft jaws, register on the finished +Z end, and indicate the prepared bore. Rough the left external diameters and complete the -Z entry counterbore without refacing the finished end.

operations.name: Pre-Spline Floor Gate
operations.setup_note: Check the soft blank at the floor station using handheld bore, diameter and axial gauges. Confirm counterbore clearance and the stock envelope needed for spline generation and subsequent tooth-pad profiling.

operations.name: Generate Internal Splines to Soft Final Size
operations.setup_note: Locate the soft blank from its prepared bore and end face in an annular fixture, with cutter entry and overtravel clear of both counterbores. Rough and finish the 28 internal teeth to the approved spline specification, establishing datum A without retaining post-hardening flank stock. NOTE: The spline must be re-gauged after heat treatment and shot blasting to verify that hardening distortion has not taken it outside tolerance. If out-of-tolerance, hard spline grinding or re-processing is required; this is a customer-decision risk.

operations.name: CNC Datum-Referenced External Finishing
operations.setup_note: Mount the soft sleeve on a pitch-contact spline arbor establishing A, with both external ends accessible; finish the outer lands and internal stepped faces before cutting the fork groove. Establish provisional E and N on the groove walls, finish those walls in the soft condition, and retain grinding allowance only on the external cylindrical surfaces. NOTE (OPEN RISK): The fork-groove side walls require Ra 0.6 per the drawing. Achieving Ra 0.6 after carburizing, quenching, and shot blasting by soft-finishing alone is a process qualification risk. Customer must confirm whether post-hardening groove-wall grinding is acceptable; if required, a separate face-grinding operation must be added to the route.

operations.name: Soft Internal Contour and Pads — Left Access
operations.setup_note: Clamp an external flange in an annular indexing fixture, pick up A with a removable spline datum gauge, and register axially from N before removing the gauge for cutter access. Machine the -Z-accessible contour and first pad locations across the 28 teeth from the controlled CAD model, roughing both feature groups before climb-finishing them.

operations.name: Soft Internal Contour and Pads — Right Access
operations.setup_note: Reverse the sleeve in the annular indexing fixture, re-establish A with the removable spline gauge, and register axially from E. Machine the +Z-accessible contour and opposite pad locations across the 28 teeth from the controlled CAD model, roughing both feature groups before climb-finishing them.

operations.name: Bench Tooth Pointing and Deburring
operations.setup_note: Hold the soft sleeve in an open-ended bench indexing fixture, referencing the spline and approved axial datum surfaces. Use a guided bench-spindle pointing tool and profile gauge for the specified tooth-end geometry, then control the local flank transitions and remove remaining machining burrs.

operations.name: Permanent Part Marking
operations.setup_note: Support the sleeve in a non-marring marking nest and apply the specified permanent identification after all soft cutting and tooth deburring. Use the approved marking location and method so identification survives hardening and shot blasting.

operations.name: Pre-Heat-Treatment Floor Gate
operations.setup_note: Use handheld spline, groove-width, profile and edge gauges at the floor station to release the completed soft parts. Verify that the marking is legible and that only the intended external cylinders retain grinding allowance.

operations.name: Pre-Heat-Treatment Clean and Dry
operations.setup_note: Place the marked sleeves in a cleaning basket, remove oil and coolant, and dry completely before furnace loading. No masking is applied under the provisional all-surface case-hardening interpretation.

operations.name: Case Carburize and Quench
operations.setup_note: Rack the clean sleeves on distortion-control ring supports with matching witness coupons and carburize followed by controlled quenching under the approved STD 1094,1 procedure. Provisionally use four qualified loads of 25 sleeves; batch certification includes case depth and core hardness.

operations.name: Temper Case-Hardened Sleeves
operations.setup_note: Transfer the quenched sleeves promptly to the qualified tempering load while retaining distortion-control support. Temper and cool to meet the specified 58–63 HRC surface hardness, retaining coupon traceability for each furnace batch.

operations.name: Post-Temper Shot Blast
operations.setup_note: Support the tempered sleeves in the qualified blasting fixture and strip quench scale and oxide before any grinding or gauging. Use controlled exposure on finished spline and groove-wall surfaces, and remove loose blast media before release.

operations.name: OD Grind External Cylindrical Surfaces
operations.setup_note: Locate the hardened sleeve on a pitch-contact spline mandrel establishing A, with axial registration from the approved groove datum and all external cylinders accessible. Grind the left rim, right rim, left shoulder, right shoulder and groove-bottom cylinder in that order, keeping the wheel clear of all groove walls and faces.

operations.name: Grinding-Burn Inspection Gate
operations.setup_note: Submit the ground sleeves to a qualified provider for nital-etch examination of every ground cylinder immediately after grinding. This is a single visual acceptance gate with no dimensional fixture, and the provider must neutralize and rinse the examined surfaces.

operations.name: Final Micro-Deburr and Clean
operations.setup_note: Support the hardened sleeve in a non-marring nest and remove only grinding-generated micro-burrs without altering the finished tooth pointing or flank transitions. Wash away abrasive residue and contaminants, then present the part clean and dry for final inspection.

operations.name: Face Grind — Fork-Groove Side Walls (Ra 0.6)
operations.setup_note: Locate on pitch-contact spline arbor and precision-grind both inner side walls of the central shift-fork groove (Datum E and N) to achieve final drawing specification of Ra 0.6. Soft finishing alone cannot reliably hold Ra 0.6 through carburizing, quenching and shot blasting.

operations.name: Final Analytical Inspection and Release
operations.setup_note: Locate the thermally stabilized sleeve in the final metrology fixture using datums A, E and N. Perform 100% gear checker verification of internal spline pitch runout, profile and tooth span to confirm zero distortion out-of-tolerance from carburizing quench. Certify hardness and case depth.

clarifications.question: What is the specified material grade for this sleeve?
clarifications.suggested_default: Provisionally plan for a carburizing-compatible steel in a soft machinable condition; do not purchase material or release the heat-treatment procedure until the grade is confirmed.

clarifications.question: What is the authoritative overall axial end-face-to-end-face length?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the extraction's provisional 31.3 mm overall length and a 40 mm sawn blank for estimating only.

clarifications.question: Is datum E the left inner wall of the fork groove rather than a detent-pad flank?
clarifications.suggested_default: Treat E as the left inner groove wall shown in Detail A.

clarifications.question: Is datum N the right inner wall of the fork groove rather than a detent-pad flank?
clarifications.suggested_default: Treat N as the right inner groove wall shown in Detail A.

clarifications.question: Can you provide the controlled internal spline specification TR-20515634?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use 28 teeth and the stated datum pitch cylinder for route estimating, but do not select a shaping cutter or manufacture a spline gauge from the incomplete extracted data.

clarifications.question: Can you supply the controlled digital shape model required by STD 101-0001?
clarifications.suggested_default: Retain CAD-driven contour and pad machining in the route without inventing omitted dimensions; production remains blocked until the model is available.

clarifications.question: Are the F13 detent pads discrete features repeated on the 28 internal teeth rather than a continuous annular feature?
clarifications.suggested_default: Treat F13 as tooth-local geometry repeated across 28 teeth, consistent with the T-T note, rather than adopting the conflicting full-circumference extraction assumption.

clarifications.question: How many axial detent-pad instances are required on each tooth?
clarifications.suggested_default: Provisionally allow two opposing pad locations per tooth, subject to confirmation by the controlled model.

clarifications.question: Can you provide the applicable revision of heat-treatment standard STD 1094,1?
clarifications.suggested_default: Provisionally route carburizing, quenching and tempering to achieve the stated case-depth and hardness requirements; induction hardening is not selected without the material-specific approved procedure.

clarifications.question: Which mutually exclusive Detail B treatment is required: the F07 radius or the F08 chamfer?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the standard F07 reference radius and omit the alternative F08 chamfer.

clarifications.question: Is final Ra 0.6 on the fork-groove side walls acceptable to achieve by soft finishing followed by controlled hardening and blasting, with no post-hardening wall grinding?
Is the finished fork-groove width 13.5 ±0.1 mm?
What is the axial depth of each Ø130 end counterbore?
Can you provide the applicable marking instruction STD 5051,16 MET 2-6-E-3?
clarifications.suggested_default: Apply permanent identification before heat treatment, but defer the marking location and execution details until the instruction is available.

clarifications.question: What cleanliness acceptance specification applies to the stated 445 cm² wetted surface?
clarifications.suggested_default: Clean and dry the complete part after finishing; quantitative cleanliness release requires the customer's acceptance specification.

clarifications.question: Is qualified subcontracted nital-etch inspection acceptable for grinding-burn verification?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use a qualified external nital-etch provider because this specific inspection capability is not listed in the shop profile.

assumptions.text: Finished sleeve overall length is 27.0 mm (13.5 mm central shift-fork groove + 2 x 6.75 mm shoulders). Recommended stock is plain rolled ring Ø160 OD × Ø110 ID × 32 mm length (2.663 kg gross weight).

The unspecified material is provisionally treated as soft carburizing-compatible steel with medium machinability. Incoming hardness is unknown; 60 HRC after tempering is an estimating representative of the specified 58–63 HRC range, not a measured result.

Normalization is included ahead of the dedicated facing stage to satisfy SHAFT-002. Furnace loading is provisionally limited to 25 parts per load; actual capacities and material-specific thermal procedures must be qualified before production.
Dedicated facing operations face the rolled ring annulus wall (radial depth 25 mm). Center drilling is eliminated as the rolled ring blank already possesses an open Ø110 mm through-bore.

The prepared bore and finished end faces provide temporary blank references before spline generation. Datum A is established by the final soft-shaped spline, after which datum-referenced external finishing is performed on a pitch-contact arbor; E and N provisionally remain the left and right groove walls respectively.

The 28-tooth applicability note takes precedence over the conflicting extraction assumption that F13 is a continuous annular pad. The provisional route allows two tooth-local pad locations per tooth and requires CAD-based stock preservation during bore preparation and shaping; cutter sweep must not remove their required raised envelope.

F09, F10 and F13 are provisionally treated as tooth-local, non-axisymmetric profiles requiring indexed multi-axis milling. Their exact geometry and accessibility must be validated from the controlled model; no spline tooth-end chamfering is assigned to either milling setup.

F07 and F08 are mutually exclusive treatments of the same corners. The standard F07 radius is selected and physically formed with the groove profile; F08 is intentionally inactive and receives no production sub-operation.

SHAFT-003 and SHAFT-004 override the standard templates: all bores, faces, internal contours and spline teeth are finished soft, with no face grinding, ID grinding, bore honing, lapping, double-disc grinding, superfinishing, tooth shaving, tooth grinding or tooth honing. No post-hardening flank stock is retained.

Post-hardening finishing is limited to external cylindrical OD grinding. The two Ø156 rims, two Ø139 shoulders and cylindrical fork-groove bottom are treated as eligible final-size external surfaces; provisionally retain 0.3 mm diametral grinding allowance, with no allowance on groove side walls or faces. The stock's 0.5 mm allowance represents general soft-machining allowance.

The groove side walls are precision-finished soft and supported through heat treatment, rather than ground afterward. Achieving final Ra 0.6 after hardening and mandatory blasting is a qualification risk requiring customer resolution; the route does not silently restore prohibited face grinding.

Carburizing, quenching and tempering are selected provisionally instead of induction hardening. All-surface case hardening is assumed because no protected soft zones are identified, so masking and unmasking are omitted unless the approved heat-treatment standard requires them.

Turning-template threading and thread relief are omitted because no threads exist. Parting off is omitted because individually sawn blanks are used; the sawn ends are explicitly finish-faced in the dedicated stage.

Milling-template datum face milling and external outline milling are replaced by turning the corresponding rotational surfaces. No separate enclosed pockets, slots, milled hole patterns, tapping or countersinking are present; the pocket-classified internal contours are produced by profile milling, and the entry counterbores are produced by boring.
Hole-making sequence eliminates Ø30 pilot drilling and Ø110 core drilling due to rolled ring hollow blank. ID machining proceeds directly by single-point rough and finish boring from Ø110 as-cut ID.

Internal spline generation uses gear shaping, not external hobbing or broaching, as required by SHAFT-004. The generation sub-operations represent rough and final soft cuts; tooth pointing and pre-hardening deburring are consolidated on the finish bench under SHAFT-008.

Quench straightening is omitted because this is a short annular sleeve, not a slender shaft; additional stress relief is omitted because it is not specified. Ring support and controlled quenching must hold the soft-finished geometry, and out-of-tolerance distortion is not assigned an unauthorized corrective process.

SHAFT-005 replaces separate post-hardening scale scrubbing with shot blasting immediately after tempering. Furnace-batch coupons certify case depth and core hardness, and SHAFT-007 consolidates the confirming hardness test with final analytical inspection rather than creating a standalone heat-treatment verification operation.

Grinding-burn examination is retained immediately after the sole grinding setup and represented as a single manual inspection gate. Qualified nital-etch capability is not explicitly listed, so it is subcontracted using the inspection machine-family key; magnetic-particle inspection is omitted because no separate drawing requirement or qualified capability is established.

Final analytical inspection is consolidated without an accompanying manual_inspect sub-operation. Profilometer measurements and cleanliness acceptance are supporting activities at that final station; non-geometric preparation, thermal processing, marking and inspection steps use empty target_feature_ids rather than claiming to cut unrelated features.
